transcriptionNote: Source transcription corrected against the original 20-page PDF. Q117 (wound watch spring) was missing; all later questions were renumbered to match the printed paper, and the duplicate erroneous final entry was removed. Q96 was corrected to the exact source wording. Independent solutions/explanations have been added through Q150 where defensible. Q7, Q9, Q10, Q16, Q25, Q26, Q46, Q60, Q61, Q62, Q108, Q133, Q138 and Q143 remain explicitly unscored with reasons. No official answer key has been supplied or verified. Q138–139 number-series explanations were checked against the printed options; Q143's degraded formula and options were recovered from the official MPSC question-paper PDF and corrected to 8 * 8 * 1 * 7 = 8 with the four printed operator sequences. Q141 remains unscored because “three times more” is ambiguous.

questions.text: Hippopotamus loves to wallow in ____ mud.
questions.explanation: “Mud” is an uncountable noun used generically, so no article is required.

questions.text: The Principal welcomed the students ____ the school.
questions.explanation: The usual construction is “welcome someone to a place”; therefore “to” fits.

questions.text: I love having ____ eggs for breakfast.
questions.explanation: “Eggs” is a plural count noun used generally, so it takes no article.

questions.text: I have ____ of things on my mind.
questions.explanation: “A lot of things” is the standard plural count-noun expression.

questions.text: The members of the choir ____ every Saturday.
questions.explanation: “Members” is plural and “every Saturday” describes a habitual action, so the verb is “meet”.

questions.text: The Aryans are ____ European stock.
questions.explanation: The idiomatic phrase is “of European stock”.

questions.text: John was ____ at the surprising turn of events.
questions.explanation: The source gives no context distinguishing “surprised” from “amazed”; both are grammatical and semantically plausible. No unique option can be defended.

questions.text: Such a gruesome event ____ never happened in the locality before.
questions.explanation: “Such an event has never happened” uses the present perfect with the singular subject “event”.

questions.text: Cleopatra was said to be an ____ beauty in her time.
questions.explanation: All four adjectives—“incomparable”, “unparalleled”, “outstanding” and “unmatched”—can describe a beauty. The sentence supplies no criterion that selects one uniquely.

questions.text: The delegates ____ since morning to meet the CEO.
questions.explanation: None of the printed options completes the sentence correctly. “Since morning” normally calls for a perfect progressive construction (for example, “have been waiting”), which is absent.

questions.text: The divers dived deep ____ the sea to locate the ship.
questions.explanation: “Dive into the sea” expresses movement from the surface to within the sea.

questions.text: By the time the concert ended, the children ____ already asleep.
questions.explanation: “By the time the concert ended” sets a past reference point; “were already asleep” is the natural past-state construction.

questions.text: Despite ____, the Judge was moved to pity.
questions.explanation: “Despite his hard-heartedness” creates the contrast explained by “the Judge was moved to pity”.

questions.text: The girls cheered ____ when their team scored a goal.
questions.explanation: “Wildly” naturally describes enthusiastic cheering after a goal.

questions.text: You've understood, ____?
questions.explanation: The positive statement “You’ve understood” takes the negative tag “haven’t you?”

questions.text: Neither of the candidates ____ for the debate.
questions.explanation: Both “shows up” (present habitual) and “showed up” (past) are grammatically possible; the item gives no time context to select the tense.

questions.text: ____ and lodging are available here.
questions.explanation: The established expression is “food and lodging”.

questions.text: Walking ____ the best way to stay fit.
questions.explanation: The sentence states a general fact; the linking verb “is” completes it.

questions.text: Because of global warming, the climate ____ changed a lot.
questions.explanation: “Has changed” is the present perfect, agreeing with the singular subject “climate”.

questions.text: Democracy without freedom is ____.
questions.explanation: Without freedom, democracy lacks an essential condition; “meaningless” completes the statement.

questions.text: He was so passionate about the job, he was like ____.
questions.explanation: “A man on a mission” conveys strong purpose and determination, matching the preceding description.

questions.text: Who ____ to apply for the post of Treasurer?
questions.explanation: “Who” refers to the singular subject seeking to apply; “wants” is the correct present-simple form.

questions.text: We can eat in the café ____ order a takeout.
questions.explanation: “Or” joins the alternatives of eating at the café and ordering takeout.

questions.text: She succeeded ____ everyone failed.
questions.explanation: “Where everyone failed” means “in the situation/place in which everyone failed”; “where” is the suitable connector.

questions.text: Choose the word that best completes the source sentence: ____.
questions.explanation: The source scan at this position does not preserve a readable question stem; only options B–D (“direct”, “wave”, “find”) can be read. The stem and option A must not be reconstructed by guesswork.

questions.text: She could not convince the jury ____ her pleas.
questions.explanation: Both “by her pleas” and “with her pleas” are acceptable ways to express the means of convincing. The options do not yield a unique answer.

questions.text: Please don't walk ____ the grass.
questions.explanation: The standard expression is “walk on the grass”.

questions.text: Good heavens! How time ____.
questions.explanation: “How time flies!” is the conventional exclamation about time passing quickly.

questions.text: Her job comes with a ____ pay package.
questions.explanation: “Hefty pay package” is the idiomatic phrase meaning a substantial or generous salary package.

questions.text: Jim was already in bed when I ____ him last night.
questions.explanation: “Last night” fixes the event in the past, so the simple past “called” is required.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The bulldozer made a humming noise. (ii) The noise irritated people nearby. (iii) They complained against the irritated bulldozer.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (ii) are complete and sensible. Statement (iii) incorrectly says the bulldozer itself was irritated; the noise irritated people.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The guests were treated to a lavish meal. (ii) They ate until they were full. (iii) That dinner party was talked about for a long time.
questions.explanation: All three sentences are grammatical and logically connected: the guests received a lavish meal, ate their fill, and the party was discussed later.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Ram was known for his eloquence. (ii) Ram was invited to speech on the meeting. (iii) At the last minute, he had to cancel the program.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (iii) are grammatical. Statement (ii) needs “invited to give a speech” or “invited to speak at the meeting”.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The aeroplane glided smooth in the blue sky. (ii) The passengers leaned back in their seats. (iii) It was such a comfortable flight.
questions.explanation: Statements (ii) and (iii) are correct. In (i), “smooth” must be the adverb “smoothly” to modify “glided”.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) John is such a good swimmer. (ii) He could swam in any sea. (iii) He once swam in the English Channel.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (iii) are correct. After the modal “could”, the base form “swim” is required, not “swam”.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Isn't he the Principal of the school? (ii) I heard that he's a man of integrity. (iii) He combines strictness with approachability.
questions.explanation: All three are grammatically sound: a question, a report of someone's integrity, and a description of his leadership style.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Can you do me favor? (ii) Can you favor me? (iii) Can you do me this favor please?
questions.explanation: Statements (ii) and (iii) are correct. Statement (i) is missing the article “a” before “favor”.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) He told us a very interesting story. (ii) The interesting listeners were captivated. (iii) Nobody wanted the story to end.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (iii) are correct. In (ii), people are “interested”; “interesting” describes something that causes interest.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) How many books do you wish to buy? (ii) How many books did she wish to buy? (iii) You wish to buy books how many?
questions.explanation: Questions (i) and (ii) have correct interrogative word order. Statement (iii) places “how many” incorrectly.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Jim was the monitor in class for five years. (ii) Jim was the class monitor for five years. (iii) Jim had been a class monitor for five years.
questions.explanation: All three constructions are grammatical ways of describing a five-year period as class monitor; (iii) uses the past perfect for a period viewed from a later past point.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) I've never seen a tiger at close range. (ii) I've never seen a tiger this close. (iii) I've never seen a tiger close up.
questions.explanation: All three expressions—“at close range”, “this close” and “close up”—are grammatical ways to describe seeing a tiger nearby.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) She's a famous actress of yesteryears. (ii) She's a famous actress yesterday. (iii) She was once a famous actress.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (iii) are grammatical. Statement (ii) incorrectly uses “yesterday” as a time modifier for a present-tense claim about fame.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) After the harvest, the farmer went to bed happy. (ii) The good harvest made the farmer happy. (iii) After the harvest, the farmer went happy to bed.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (ii) are grammatical. In (iii), “happy” is placed unnaturally after “went”; the idiomatic construction is “went to bed happy”.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The current is too strong to cross. (ii) The current is too wide to cross. (iii) The current is too powerful to cross.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (iii) express that the flow is too forceful to cross. “Too wide” does not naturally describe a current; width describes the watercourse.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The Sun is too heat today. (ii) The Sun is too hot today. (iii) The Sun is so hot today.
questions.explanation: Statements (ii) and (iii) are correct. “Heat” in (i) is a noun; the adjective needed after “is” is “hot”.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Don't you have anything better to do? (ii) Don't you have anything to do with your time? (iii) Don't you have anything useful to do?
questions.explanation: The wording of statement (ii) is awkward, but it can be read as a grammatical rhetorical question about how someone uses their time. The distinction between a stylistic preference and a grammatical error is not sufficiently clear to select a unique combination confidently.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) For heaven's sake, stop wasting your time! (ii) For heaven's sake, stop waste time! (iii) For heaven's sake, stop wasting time!
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (iii) are correct. The imperative “stop” takes a gerund here (“wasting”), not the bare noun/verb “waste”.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) She's a strong, confident woman. (ii) She exudes confident. (iii) Her confidence is admired by many.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (iii) are correct. “Exudes” requires the noun “confidence”, not the adjective “confident”.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) Which pairs of shoes do you prefer? (ii) Which pair of shoes do you prefer? (iii) Which of these pairs do you prefer?
questions.explanation: All three questions are grammatical: “pairs” can be plural, “pair” can refer to one pair, and “these pairs” points to a set already identified.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentences: (i) The restaurant opens at all hours. (ii) The restaurant opens 24x7. (iii) The restaurant is opening at all times.
questions.explanation: Statements (i) and (ii) are acceptable ways to describe a restaurant's continuous opening hours. Statement (iii) uses an unnatural progressive form for a regular schedule.

questions.text: His most trusted friend proved to be a snake in the grass.
questions.explanation: A “snake in the grass” is a concealed enemy or treacherous person; “a hidden enemy” is the closest option.

questions.text: You cannot have your cake and eat it too.
options: make the best of a situation
questions.explanation: The idiom means one cannot enjoy two mutually incompatible advantages; in other words, one cannot “have it both ways”.

questions.text: The cashier wiped the nose of his employer by presenting false bills.
questions.explanation: To “wipe the nose” of someone in this context means to cheat or defraud that person.

questions.text: After the death of his father, the son played ducks and drakes with his inherited property.
questions.explanation: “Play ducks and drakes with” property means to squander or spend it recklessly; “spend lavishly” is the closest option.

questions.text: After his retirement, Mr. Dave is thinking of resting on his oars.
questions.explanation: “Rest on one's oars” means to stop striving after previous effort or achievement; “resting after hard work” is the closest option.

questions.text: Easy to shape in desired form
questions.explanation: “Malleable” means capable of being shaped or formed easily.

questions.text: Very pleasing to eat
questions.explanation: “Luscious” describes food that is richly pleasant or delicious to taste.

questions.text: One who desires freedom from control, especially government control
questions.explanation: An “anarchist” advocates the absence of imposed governmental control or authority.

questions.text: Beyond all power of destruction of time
questions.explanation: “Imperishable” means not liable to perish or be destroyed by the passage of time.

questions.text: Composed of elements highly diverse in character
questions.explanation: The definition calls for the adjective “heterogeneous” (made up of diverse elements), but that word is absent. “Heterogeneity” names the condition, not the thing composed of diverse elements; the remaining options do not fit. No option is defensible.

questions.text: Punctilious (word appears OCR-corrupted in the source)
questions.explanation: The source scan renders the bold headword as “hrnctilious”; although the likely intended word is “punctilious”, its exact printed spelling cannot be confirmed from the available page extraction. Keep unscored pending clearer source image.

questions.text: Mendacious (word appears OCR-corrupted in the source)
questions.explanation: The source scan renders the bold headword as “Meadaclous”; “mendacious” is a plausible intended word given option C, but the printed headword cannot be confirmed. Keep unscored pending clearer source image.

questions.text: Ameliorate
questions.explanation: “Ameliorate” means to make something better or improve it.

questions.text: Cursory
questions.explanation: “Cursory” means hasty or superficial; “casual” is the closest available synonym.

questions.text: Implicate
questions.explanation: To “implicate” someone is to involve or show that person to be connected with something, often wrongdoing.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'Selfish' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: “Selfless” is the opposite of “selfish”: it describes concern for others rather than oneself.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'Comfortable' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: “Uncomfortable” is the direct opposite of “comfortable”.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'Important' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: “Trivial” means insignificant, the opposite of “important” in this context.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'Underestimate'.
questions.explanation: To “overestimate” is the opposite of to “underestimate”.

questions.text: Choose the antonym of 'Decayed'.
questions.explanation: “Thriving” means flourishing or prospering, the opposite of having decayed.

questions.text: Choose the meaning of 'Breeding place' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: In the passage, the home is described as the place where children are shaped; a “formative space” best captures “breeding place” in this context.

questions.text: Choose the meaning of 'Pander' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: To “pander” to someone's whims is to give in to or indulge their demands.

questions.text: Choose the meaning of 'Symptom' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: A “symptom” is an observable sign or indication of something.

questions.text: Choose the meaning of 'Society at large' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: “Society at large” means the wider or greater community, not only a family, home or neighbourhood.

questions.text: Choose the meaning of 'Lifestyle' in the context of the passage.
questions.explanation: “Lifestyle” means a person's or group's way of life.

questions.text: Which of the following rulers issued copper coins named 'Uital'?
questions.explanation: Iltutmish introduced the silver tanka and copper jital coinage; the copper jital is the coin referred to in the question.

questions.text: Which canyon is known as the 'Grand Canyon' of India or the Arizona of India?
questions.explanation: Gandikota Canyon in Andhra Pradesh is commonly called the Grand Canyon of India.

questions.text: Population dividend means
options: the total population of the world
migration of the people from poorer region to richer region
the total number of population above 65 years
the youthful age structure of a population
questions.explanation: The demographic dividend refers to the economic potential associated with a youthful age structure and a relatively large working-age population.

questions.text: Which of the given vitamins is a water-soluble vitamin?
questions.explanation: B-complex vitamins are water-soluble; vitamins A, K and D are fat-soluble.

questions.text: The Summer Olympics 2020 was hosted by Japan. The Summer Olympics 2024 was hosted by
questions.explanation: The 2024 Summer Olympic Games were hosted by France, with Paris as the principal host city.

questions.text: Entomology is the science that studies
options: the origin and history of technical and scientific terms
questions.explanation: Entomology is the branch of zoology concerned with insects.

questions.text: The tallest statue in the world, the Statue of Unity, is located near which dam?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Unity stands near the Sardar Sarovar Dam on the Narmada River.

questions.text: Grand Central Terminal, Park Avenue, New York is the world's
questions.explanation: Grand Central Terminal in New York is widely described as the world's largest railway station by number of platforms and tracks; that is the intended sense of “largest” here.

questions.text: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change deals with
questions.explanation: The UN Framework Convention on Climate Change addresses climate change by seeking to stabilise greenhouse-gas concentrations; the option on greenhouse-gas emission mitigation is the closest.

questions.text: The only drone station in Meghalaya is located in
questions.explanation: The State's dedicated healthcare drone station is at Jengjal Sub-divisional Hospital in West Garo Hills, so the matching option is Garo Hills.

questions.text: Which of the following countries is not a member of the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (QSD or QUAD)?
questions.explanation: The Quad consists of Australia, India, Japan and the United States. The United Kingdom is not a member.

questions.text: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope was launched into space on
questions.explanation: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope launched on 25 December 2021.

questions.text: The unit of electrical resistance of a conductor is
questions.explanation: Electrical resistance is measured in ohms, symbol Ω.

questions.text: Hockey was introduced in the Asian Games in
questions.explanation: Men's field hockey was introduced at the 1958 Asian Games in Tokyo.

questions.text: Which treaty ended the Anglo-Sikh War?
options: The Treaty of Peace of Paris
questions.explanation: The First Anglo-Sikh War ended with the Treaty of Lahore in 1846.

questions.text: Rangaswamy Cup is associated with
questions.explanation: The Rangaswamy Cup is associated with field hockey.

questions.text: India's longest bridge, Dhola-Sadiya Bridge, was built over which tributary of the Brahmaputra River?
questions.explanation: The Dhola–Sadiya (Bhupen Hazarika Setu) bridge crosses the Lohit River, a major tributary of the Brahmaputra.

questions.text: Which country launched the world's first nationwide 5G mobile network?
questions.explanation: South Korea launched the first nationwide commercial 5G network in April 2019.

questions.text: Who among the following inaugurated the 'Greater Sohra Water Supply Scheme' in Meghalaya?
questions.explanation: The Greater Sohra Water Supply Scheme was inaugurated by Union Jal Shakti Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat.

questions.text: In which year did the Goods and Services Tax (GST) come into effect in India?
questions.explanation: India's Goods and Services Tax came into effect on 1 July 2017.

questions.text: Where in the world did the game of lawn tennis originate?
questions.explanation: The source asks where lawn tennis originated, not in which year. Birmingham is the intended option among the listed cities.

questions.text: Who introduced 'Green Army' for environmental conservation?
questions.explanation: The Green Army environmental-conservation programme was introduced in Australia as a youth environmental work programme.

questions.text: The first pico-satellite of India is
questions.explanation: ANUSAT, built by Anna University, is recognised as India's first university-built pico-satellite.

questions.text: The alliance among Brazil, Germany, India and Japan to support each other's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) is called
questions.explanation: Brazil, Germany, India and Japan form the G4 grouping, which supports one another's bids for permanent UNSC seats.

questions.text: The 'Miyawaki method' is well known for
options: promotion of commercial farming in arid and semi-arid areas
development of gardens using genetically modified flora
creating mini forests in urban areas
harvesting wind energy on coastal areas and sea surfaces
questions.explanation: The Miyawaki method is used to establish dense, fast-growing native mini-forests, including in urban spaces.

questions.text: Which State in India has the longest coastline?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has India's longest coastline among the states.

questions.text: Who coined the slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad'?
questions.explanation: The slogan “Inquilab Zindabad” was coined by Maulana Hasrat Mohani; Bhagat Singh later popularised it.

questions.text: Which is the first bank to introduce ATM in India?
questions.explanation: HSBC introduced India's first ATM in Mumbai in 1987.

questions.text: The philosophical study of beliefs and knowledge is better known as
questions.explanation: Epistemology is the branch of philosophy that studies knowledge and the nature and justification of belief.

questions.text: Which Indian cricketer became the first woman to score a double century in Test cricket?
questions.explanation: Mithali Raj scored 214 against England in 2002, becoming the first woman to score a double century in a Test match.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book The Little Book of Encouragement?
questions.explanation: The Little Book of Encouragement is attributed to the Dalai Lama.

questions.text: The State Flower of Meghalaya is
questions.explanation: Meghalaya's state flower is the Lady's Slipper Orchid.

questions.text: Which space agency launched its first civilian mission to space?
questions.explanation: The stem calls the organisation a “space agency”, but SpaceX (the only option associated with the first all-civilian orbital mission, Inspiration4) is a private aerospace company, not a space agency. The question's premise and category are inconsistent, so no option can be defended as written.

questions.text: Birju Maharaj, who expired on 17th January, 2022, was an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Birju Maharaj was a leading exponent of Kathak, the North Indian classical dance form.

questions.text: Which social media platform launched a feature named 'Tip Jar' which enables users to send money to their favourite accounts?
questions.explanation: Twitter introduced Tip Jar as a feature allowing users to send money to accounts they wished to support.

questions.text: Which one of the following became the first State to table a paperless budget in India?
questions.explanation: Meghalaya became the first Indian state to present a paperless budget, in 2021.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the first country to approve the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine?
questions.explanation: The United Kingdom was the first country to authorise the Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine for use.

questions.text: Parakram Diwas is observed to celebrate the birth anniversary of
options: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
questions.explanation: Parakram Diwas is observed on 23 January, the birth anniversary of Subhas Chandra Bose.

questions.text: Which State Government developed the world's largest floating solar project on Narmada River?
questions.explanation: The Narmada floating-solar project referenced in the question was developed by the Madhya Pradesh government.

questions.text: National Youth Day is celebrated on
questions.explanation: National Youth Day is observed on 12 January, the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.

questions.text: Where was the first major public appearance of Mahatma Gandhi in India in February 1916?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's first major public appearance in India after returning from South Africa was at the inauguration of Banaras Hindu University in February 1916.

questions.text: A wound watch spring has ____ energy.
questions.explanation: A wound spring stores elastic potential energy. It releases that stored energy as it unwinds.

questions.text: When water freezes, its density
questions.explanation: When water freezes, it expands; the same mass occupies more volume, so its density decreases.

questions.text: The term URL used in internet technology stands for
questions.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, the address used to identify a resource on the internet.

questions.text: India and Sri Lanka are divided by the
questions.explanation: India and Sri Lanka are separated by the Palk Strait.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct regarding Gross Domestic Savings in India?
options: Contribution of the Household Sector is the largest
Contribution of the Government Sector is the largest
Contribution of the Corporate Sector is the largest
Contribution of the Agricultural Sector is the largest
questions.explanation: The household sector is the largest contributor to gross domestic savings in India.

questions.text: Which of the following sports involves animals?
questions.explanation: Jallikattu is a traditional sport involving bulls, so it is the animal-related sport among the options.

questions.text: 'Sangai' festival is celebrated in which of the following Indian States?
questions.explanation: The Sangai Festival is celebrated in Manipur.

questions.text: Avani Lekhara became the first Indian woman to win two Paralympic medals at the Tokyo Paralympics, 2020. Which of the following was her discipline?
questions.explanation: Avani Lekhara is a rifle-shooting athlete; she won two medals at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics.

questions.text: Chronologically arrange the following Indian-origin astronauts on the basis of their flying into space, starting with the first.
options: Sunita Williams, Kalpana Chawla, Sirisha Bandla, Rakesh Sharma
Rakesh Sharma, Kalpana Chawla, Sunita Williams, Sirisha Bandla
Rakesh Sharma, Sunita Williams, Kalpana Chawla, Sirisha Bandla
Kalpana Chawla, Sirisha Bandla, Rakesh Sharma, Sunita Williams
questions.explanation: Rakesh Sharma flew in 1984, Kalpana Chawla in 1997, Sunita Williams in 2006 and Sirisha Bandla in 2021; option B gives this order.

questions.text: In a line of 45 students, Amit is 10th from the left end and Mary is 15th from the right end. How many students are between Amit and Mary?
questions.explanation: Mary is 15th from the right, or 31st from the left (45 − 15 + 1). There are 31 − 10 − 1 = 20 students between them.

questions.text: Find the smaller angle made by an hour and minute hand at 10:20.
questions.explanation: At 10:20, the minute hand is at 120° and the hour hand at 310°. Their smaller separation is 360° − 190° = 170°.

questions.text: If Sunita celebrated her wedding anniversary on Tuesday, 30th September, 1997, when will she celebrate her next wedding anniversary on the same day?
questions.explanation: The date 30 September falls on Tuesday again in 2003: the intervening common and leap-year shifts total six weekdays.

questions.text: Four metal rods of lengths 78 cm, 104 cm, 117 cm and 169 cm are to be cut into parts of equal length. Each part must be as long as possible. The maximum number of pieces that can be obtained will be
questions.explanation: The greatest equal segment length is HCF(78, 104, 117, 169) = 13 cm. The pieces are 6 + 8 + 9 + 13 = 36.

questions.text: In the series given below, a number is missing. Find the missing number: 91, 73, ?, 43, 31, 21.
questions.explanation: The missing term is 57: the sequence follows n² − (n−1), descending from 10²−9=91 to 5²−4=21.

questions.text: If in a certain code, E = 5, HOTEL = 12, then how will the word LAMB be represented?
questions.explanation: The code is the average of the letters' alphabetical positions: HOTEL totals 60, giving 12. LAMB totals 28; 28 ÷ 4 = 7.

questions.text: Pointing to a man in a photograph, Nisha said, 'He is the brother of the daughter of the wife of my husband.' How is the man in the photograph related to Nisha?
questions.explanation: The brother of Nisha's daughter is Nisha's son, so the man is her son.

questions.text: A tourist covers half of her journey by train at 50 km/h, half of the remainder by bus at 30 km/h and the rest by cycle at 10 km/h. The average speed of the tourist during the journey is
questions.explanation: For equal total distance, the travel times are d/100, d/120 and d/40 hours. The average speed is 300/13 ≈ 23.08 km/h, but none of the four options is 23.08. Option 24 is only an approximation and the paper gives no rounding instruction; leave unscored.

questions.text: In a certain code, '253' means 'books are old', '546' means 'man is old' and '378' means 'buy good books'. What stands for 'are' in that code?
questions.explanation: The common digit in 253 and 546 represents “old” (5). The common digit in 253 and 378 represents “books” (3). Therefore 2 represents “are”.

questions.text: Five friends are sitting on a bench. A is to the left of B but on the right of C. D is to the right of B but on the left of E. Who are sitting at the extremes of the bench?
questions.explanation: The order from left to right is C–A–B–D–E, so C and E occupy the two extremes.

questions.text: A and B start walking from the same point. A goes North and covers 3 km, then turns right and covers 4 km. B goes West and covers 5 km and then turns right and covers 3 km. How far apart are they from each other?
questions.explanation: A finishes at (4, 3). B travels west 5 km and then north 3 km, finishing at (−5, 3). Their horizontal separation is 9 km.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a circle facing the centre. H is fourth to the left of B and second to the right of F. A is third to the left of C, who is not an immediate neighbour of F. G is second to the left of A. D is second to the right of E. Who is on the immediate right of F?
questions.explanation: The valid differences are 64, 32, 16, 8, 4 and 2. After 192 the next term should be 196, not 194; therefore 194 is the wrong number.

questions.text: Find the wrong number in the following number series: 72, 136, 168, 184, 192, 194, 198.
questions.explanation: The successive differences should halve: 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2. After 192 the next term should be 196, not 194. Therefore 194 (option B) is the wrong number.

questions.text: Find the wrong number in the following number series: 21, 30, 37, 55, 85, 131, 197.
questions.explanation: The intended successive differences are consecutive squares: 3², 4², 5², 6², 7², 8². The series should be 21, 30, 46, 71, 107, 156, 220; the printed 37 is the first term that breaks the pattern. Option B is 37.

questions.text: The sum of the ages of a daughter and mother is 56 years. After four years, the age of the mother will be three times the age of the daughter. What is the age of the daughter and mother respectively?
questions.explanation: Let the daughter's age be d and the mother's age be m. d+m=56 and m+4=3(d+4), giving d=12 and m=44.

questions.text: Father is aged three times more than his son Ronald. After 8 years, he would be two and a half times Ronald's age. After another 16 years, how many times would he be of Ronald's age?
questions.explanation: The phrase “three times more than his son” is ambiguous: it can be read as three times the son's age or as four times the son's age. Those interpretations produce different results, and the wording does not clarify which is intended. No option is defensible without assuming the setter's intended meaning.

questions.text: A total of 324 notes comprising ₹20 and ₹50 denominations make a sum of ₹12,450. The total number of ₹20 notes is
questions.explanation: Let x be the number of ₹20 notes and y the number of ₹50 notes. x+y=324 and 20x+50y=12,450; solving gives x=125.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the '*' signs and balance the following equation: 8 * 8 * 1 * 7 = 8
questions.explanation: Using division and multiplication from left to right, 8 ÷ 8 × 1 + 7 = 1 + 7 = 8. The correct sequence is ÷, ×, + (option C).

questions.text: Johnny walked 25 m towards South. Then he turned to his left and walked 20 m. He then turned to his left and walked 25 m. He again turned to his right and walked 15 m. At what distance is he from his starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation: He walks 25 m south, 20 m east, 25 m north and 15 m east. The north–south movement cancels; he is 35 m east of the start.

questions.text: Given below are two statements followed by two conclusions. Consider the statements true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Statements: I. Health Insurance in India caters only to the rich. II. Health Insurance Sector should be regularized. Conclusions: I. Health Insurance Sector should be nationalized. II. Health Insurance is not required for the poor. Which conclusion follows?
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Neither conclusion follows. The statements do not imply that health insurance should be nationalised or that poor people do not need it.

questions.text: Given below are three statements followed by two conclusions. Statements: I. All shoes are pens. II. Some pens are razors. III. Some razors are desks. Conclusions: I. Some desks are shoes. II. Some razors are shoes. Which conclusion(s) follow?
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: All shoes are pens, but the “some pens are razors” group need not contain shoes. Likewise, the “some razors are desks” group need not contain shoes. Neither conclusion is guaranteed.

questions.text: Danny introduced Wilburn as the son of the only brother of his father's wife. How is Wilburn related to Danny?
questions.explanation: The person is the son of his father's wife's brother—his paternal uncle's son, i.e. his cousin.

questions.text: Select the related letters from the given alternatives: Bbc : cBB :: Llm : ?
questions.explanation: The pattern reverses the letter order and presents the final two letters in capitals: Bbc becomes cBB, so Llm becomes mLL.

questions.text: If 1st January is a Friday, then what is the first day of the month of March in a leap year?
questions.explanation: In a leap year, January has 31 days and February has 29. Starting with Friday on 1 January, 1 March is Tuesday.

questions.text: Which is the smallest in value among the following numbers? (The superscript notation is unclear in the source scan.)
questions.explanation: Comparing the powers by logarithms: 2²⁵⁰≈10⁷⁵·²⁵, 3¹⁵⁰≈10⁷¹·⁵⁶, 5¹⁰⁰≈10⁶⁹·⁹⁹ and 4²⁰⁰≈10¹²⁰·⁴; 5¹⁰⁰ is smallest.
